value: SAME_LAB_AS (recall-oriented) = shared corresponding / senior author OR the same affiliation unit within +-N years; N = 3 (set by the signer 2026-10-26). lab_group_id is MANDATORY (status UNKNOWN allowed) for KIN and for DRV with a KIN parent; where authorship was not read, lab_group_status = UNKNOWN and the series is not SIM-VAL / DS-TEST eligible
rationale: AGENT DRAFT from review B #4. Steps 11 / 26 / 27 / 32 use the lab group as the unit of independence (CHG-11-3); the quotas and the VAL-5 group count cannot be computed unless authorship is stored (DOC.authorship). B0 descriptive group counts (39.0% / 39.4% shares) were known to the drafter; no lineage component, edge or label is computed.

quantity: Compilation membership screen status and the NOT_INDEPENDENT_VERIFIED label

rationale: AGENT DRAFT from review B #3. USDA R6 and Bognar are compiled from primary papers that Steps 10-14 will acquire; 'no bibliography means implicit independence' is the wrong default for a recall-oriented design. Mirrors G08-9 (THR-08A-11). B0 descriptive group counts (39.0% / 39.4% shares) were known to the drafter; no lineage component, edge or label is computed.

rationale: AGENT DRAFT. It labels, it does not decide whether a series is stored (that is THR-04K-01). No data seen.

rationale: AGENT DRAFT from review B #16 (rule, no number beyond 2). Reproducibility and error propagation of a figure read need axis scale, calibration points, digitizer identity and repeat reads. No data seen.

quantity: Grouping and one-per-group
value: at most 1 recipe per split_group_id (07I-S SPLITGRP-REC-) or, before it exists, per connected component of exact duplicate group + provisional family + dish-family candidate + same normalised title; if a component with an excluded id exceeds S_max = 500 recipes exclude only exact/family/title-tied members

rationale: Count-only index fixed before the draw; round cutpoints; every tier is populated in each source (frame counts read). Not tuned to any outcome.

quantity: P1 cells (stratum x source x tier)
value: baking FOODCOM MID; drain_discard BBC LOW; indian WIKIBOOKS MID; multi_component FOODCOM HIGH; random BBC MID; reserve_split FOODCOM HIGH; simple WIKIBOOKS LOW. Strata regexes exactly as tools/make_gold_batch.py; indian = explicit cuisine label Indian/Indic; fall-through order FOODCOM -> BBC -> WIKIBOOKS if a cell has < 30 eligible

value: seed = first 8 bytes of SHA-256(frame_sha256 || wave label || human nonce written into the signed row before the frame is built); stable shuffle inside each cell; first unused-group candidate is drawn; the next 2 per cell are ordered reserves

quantity: Hard-case coverage
value: reported, not enforced: P2 chosen by seeded greedy coverage of mechanically taggable SSOT s237.5 classes; classes with 0 occurrences are listed UNCOVERED; no redraw for coverage
rationale: Card says "checked against the s237.5 list". Redrawing for coverage would tune the sample to the schema. P2 is therefore coverage-enriched (open decision D19-10).
signed_by: Kush Tokas; Parv Goyal (Parv's ok relayed by Kush)

quantity: Provenance-validity checks (counts_as_pilot_provenance)
value: FAIL: identical file bytes (PV-1); recorded mtime (written into the commitment at commitment time) outside the timing-sheet window or after the commitment (PV-3); commitment after the sealed key was opened (PV-6); a commitments file not tracked in git, or committed after the sealed key was opened (PV-9). REVIEW: identical normalised label content in > 10% of recipes (PV-2); active minutes < 5 per recipe (PV-4); authorship not separate (PV-5); a field with >= 100 cells and dominant-class share < 0.95 with >= 98% identical codes and identical marginals, or a field with dominant-class share >= 0.95 with chance-corrected identity (p_o - p_e) / (1 - p_e) >= 0.98 on >= 100 cells (PV-7); a label file with fewer than 2 hashed interim snapshots or a final snapshot hash different from the committed hash (PV-10)
rationale: Pattern of step07h_human_gate_result.json (counts_as_human_gate): two files 11 s apart, 899/900 cells identical. FAIL => wave NOT_COUNTED (07H precedent). The five-minute and 98% values are plausibility floors, not literature values. Round-3 changes: PV-3 runs on values recorded at commitment (file mtimes do not survive git checkout, cp or scp and are forgeable by touch); PV-9 adds a git timestamp that someone other than the annotator can check; PV-10 adds an interim history against whole-file copies; PV-7 is chance-corrected for high-prevalence fields so it does not fire on natural near-identity (a field with p_e = 1 is skipped and listed, not dropped). Every earlier trigger remains.
signed_by: Kush Tokas; Parv Goyal (Parv's ok relayed by Kush)

quantity: Planted-pair test of the provenance checker
value: 100% detection of a planted identical-file pair, a planted 11-second pair, a planted identical-content pair, a planted commitments file not tracked in git (PV-9 FAIL) and a planted label file without interim snapshots (PV-10 REVIEW); 0 false positives on a planted clean pair; the checker is unusable until this passes
rationale: Card pass gate G19.P(1) requires a planted-pair unit test.
signed_by: Kush Tokas; Parv Goyal (Parv's ok relayed by Kush)

quantity: Per-recipe time-box
value: 120 active minutes; on reaching it the annotator stops, marks TIMEBOX_EXCEEDED, logs a schema problem; time is right-censored and reported with and without
rationale: Prevents one recipe from consuming the cap; a recipe that does not fit is a finding about depth. 120 min = upper end of the Deep Gold 30-90 min estimate plus 30 min.

rationale: Plan card G19.P(5), unchanged. Setup 1 h added by this draft.
signed_by: Kush Tokas; Parv Goyal (Parv's ok relayed by Kush)

value: a disagreement category > 20% of its relevant units => HANDBOOK_REVISION_REQUIRED (tools/gold_pilot_agreement.py GATE_RATE = 0.20, tool denominators); this rate is still computed and reported, and the gate fires on max(this rate, THR-19P-31 rate)
rationale: Verbatim existing rule (S102 gate). The tool sums both annotators' units in most denominators, so the rule is harder to trigger than a per-pair reading (up to 2x on matched-pair rows); THR-19P-31 adds the per-pair rate to the gate. This row is not weakened: every case it flags is still flagged.

quantity: Core vs secondary field classes
value: core: ingredient-line spans, canonical concept link, quantity structure, ACTION/process mapping, event structure, merge/split/reserve/recombine relations; secondary: coreference, intermediate/alive entities, final state attributes, implicit events
rationale: Plan PP split (core >= 0.80; state attributes and implicit args >= 0.667). Definition of "core" for the pilot falsification rule. Routing quantity per family: alpha for categorical families (THR-19P-18), F1 for span / event / edge / coreference / entity families (THR-19P-35).

quantity: Routing thresholds on Krippendorff's alpha (categorical families: concept link, event type, quantity_override, final state fields)
value: alpha >= 0.80 reportable as met (diagnostic); 0.667 <= alpha < 0.80 => handbook revision and re-measure on NEW recipes; alpha < 0.667 => redesign or demote field. The F1 families are routed by THR-19P-35, not by this row
rationale: Krippendorff (2004) convention for chance-corrected agreement, used for routing only; the pilot certifies nothing. Round-3 split: the Plan card applied one pair of cut-offs to 'alpha or F1', quantities on different scales (an F1 of 0.70 and an alpha of 0.70 do not mean the same).

quantity: Confidence interval method
value: recipe-cluster bootstrap, B = 10000, percentile interval (plus BCa and cluster-level t interval, reported together; rules that read a bound use THR-19P-34), recomputed from per-recipe sufficient statistics; leave-one-recipe-out influence table; Wilson on pooled units is not primary; all intervals are conditional on annotators A and B
rationale: Units within a recipe are correlated; recipe is the unit of independence (one per split group).

rationale: Prevents interval-free claims on rare classes (reserve/recombine, implicit events).

quantity: High-prevalence rule
value: dominant-class share >= 0.95 on a categorical field => kappa and alpha printed but not interpreted; AC1 and specific agreement carry the reading
rationale: Same prevalence value as THR-07A-03; kappa paradox (Feinstein and Cicchetti 1990).

rationale: Plan: every adjudication has who / why / version (G19.M); applied to the pilot.

quantity: Schema-problem triage completeness

quantity: STOP-SCHEMA by blocking items logged by both annotators (retained as a supplementary trigger; the main rule is THR-19P-32)

rationale: Operationalises "schema incoherent" (M.10) for a pilot; BLOCKING = cannot annotate faithfully without inventing or dropping content. Zero BLOCKING in 20 recipes bounds the per-recipe rate only at 13.9% (one-sided 95%). Retained unchanged as a supplementary trigger because it needs convergence and three coarse categories, so it under-detects (Review B 19-2); THR-19P-32 is the primary rule and no trigger is removed.

rationale: Only N <= 40 is within the current mandate (MP AH6); B_h is a human capacity input that does not exist in the repo.

Never an authorisation: N > 40 needs a separate H5/H8 decision; intervals are conditional on annotators A and B
rationale: The pilot cannot certify 0.80 with n = 20; the rule only says when it is reasonable to ask.

quantity: Handbook review gate on the per-pair-normalised rate (supersedes THR-19P-16 for gating)
value: HANDBOOK_REVISION_REQUIRED if max(tool rate, per-pair-normalised rate) > 0.20 for any disagreement category; per-pair rate = category rows / units of ONE annotator (half the tool's summed denominator where it sums both annotators; the mean of the two counts if they differ)

quantity: STOP-SCHEMA by adjudicated blocking items, any logger
value: >= 2 recipes each carrying an adjudicated schema-problem item with adjudication_class SCHEMA_GAP or HANDBOOK_GAP and severity BLOCKING on the same field family => STOP-SCHEMA for that family (escalate to Step 16), whoever logged it; a single-annotator BLOCKING item may be downgraded or dismissed only with a written rationale and every dismissed BLOCKING item is listed in the report
rationale: Operationalises 'schema incoherent' without requiring both annotators to log the same three categories (THR-19P-26 needs convergence and a high bar, so a problem seen by one careful annotator never counts). quantity: Per-recipe representability checklist and silent schema debt
value: after labelling each recipe and before commitment each annotator marks every hard-case class present (handbook hard-example list = SSOT 237.5 classes) FAITHFUL / WORKAROUND / IMPOSSIBLE plus one free OTHER row; IMPOSSIBLE = a BLOCKING log item; WORKAROUND counts are reported as silent schema debt next to BLOCKING; the sheet is private until both commitments and its hash is committed
rationale: Makes under-detection of schema problems visible (Review B 19-2). Reporting rule; no pass threshold, no gate is weakened. The analyst-only known-gap list stays sealed so the checklist does not prime annotators.
signed_by: Kush Tokas; Parv Goyal (Parv's ok relayed by Kush)

quantity: Interval rule for decisions that read a bound
value: for each statistic compute the percentile cluster bootstrap, the BCa cluster bootstrap and a cluster-level t interval on per-recipe statistics (df = n_recipes - 1); any rule that reads a lower bound uses the smallest lower limit, any rule that reads an upper bound the largest upper limit; all three are reported; 7-recipe intervals stay 'indicative only'; all intervals are conditional on annotators A and B
rationale: Percentile intervals undercover with few clusters (stated for 7, equally true for 13); the pilot has exactly two fixed annotators who wrote the handbook, so no interval estimates annotator variance. Choosing the more conservative limit can only make a pass harder.
signed_by: Kush Tokas; Parv Goyal (Parv's ok relayed by Kush)
ci_rule: min / max of percentile, BCa and cluster-t limits

quantity: Routing thresholds on F1 (span, event, edge, coreference, entity families); routing convention only
value: F1 >= 0.80 reportable as met (diagnostic); 0.667 <= F1 < 0.80 => handbook revision and re-measure on NEW recipes; F1 < 0.667 => redesign or demote field. F1 is not chance-corrected (for spans it equals positive specific agreement): the Krippendorff cut-offs are borrowed as a routing convention, an F1 of x is never read as an alpha of x and no F1 supports a reliability claim; unitizing alpha is an optional diagnostic and is not routed on
rationale: Round-3 split of THR-19P-18 (Review B 19-1): the same numeric cut-offs are kept, so no gate is weakened, but they are labelled for what they are on this scale.
